item.title: Why is the Cheesecake Factory at the center of the latest culture war?
item.description: A joke by former President Obama has gone viral and received backlash from the Trump administration as the issue of affordability looms large over next week's midterm elections.

item.title: Binance flags 'potential security issue,' says approximately $6.3 billion impacted
item.description: It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are "working around the clock" to resolve the issue.

item.title: Candy prices got you scared stiff? What to know about the cost of Halloween this year
item.description: Prices for candy, the most popular Halloween purchase, and gum have risen 7.7% in one year and are up more than 18% in two years, according to the latest federal data.

item.title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
item.description: The websites of unknown origin are targeting key U.S. House races. They are getting picked up by ChatGPT's responses but Google's products avoid promoting them.

item.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
item.description: Most kids say they use chatbots for help with homework and when they're stressed, lonely, or anxious. And how they use chatbots is tied to their mental health.

item.title: Trump's VA killed a home loan program. Thousands of veterans are paying the price
item.description: An NPR investigation finds that more than 15,000 military veterans were put into much-higher-cost home loans after the Trump administration cut a key program. Many now pay $1,000 more per month.
item.content:encoded:
An NPR investigation finds that more than 15,000 military veterans were put into much-higher-cost home loans after the Trump administration cut a key program. Many now pay $1,000 more per month.

(Image credit: Maddie McGarvey for NPR)

item.title: 'Affordability? For who?' Voters decide between helping homeowners or public services
item.description: Candidates across the U.S. have paid lip service to affordability issues. In Florida, the question of how to save voters money, and at what cost, is literally on the ballot.
